whatItFakes: A state's fiscal laws (a balanced operating budget, funding pensions to schedule, a minimum reserve balance) move what it pays to borrow (the outcome web's gov.borrowing-cost, in basis points), and the treasury reprices the state's whole interest line by that change over the state's own rate on its debt at once, as if every bond it owes were issued at the new spread. County and city interest lines do not read it. The federal-deficit and newspaper-closure links into the same spread still do not run: the web records no change in the federal deficit, and the newspaper link has its cause now (the closed local newspapers the press module records) but no size, because the study prices a county's own bonds after its county paper closes and no county or city interest line reads the spread.
why: No record keeps a government's bonds by issue date or maturity, so the treasury cannot tell new issues from old; the research measures spreads on state general-obligation bonds only.
replacement: A bond record per government (issue date, amount, coupon, maturity) from the Census debt outstanding, with new issues priced at the spread the web keeps, so a law's change reaches only the bonds issued after it, and local governments' spreads read the same measure.

whatItFakes: The loan-rate-cap links move the count of consumer lenders (payday, title and installment) per 100,000 residents.
why: The credit engine lends one product, the town bank's personal loan at prime plus spread, which never reaches a high-cost rate; there is no payday or title lender, and the cap law already ceilings that loan's rate in householdApplications.
replacement: Resolved Oct 29 (world-small-dollar-lenders): the credit engine's small-dollar lender is the high-cost lender product, and it reads the web's factor on finance.high-cost-loans through webReach where it quotes a loan (householdApplications in src/core2/modules/credit.ts), so the loan-rate-cap links change what it lends.

whatItFakes: Fix-it-first moves the share of roads in poor condition; the share is kept only in the web.
why: No engine keeps road condition: setRoadCondition in place-prices.ts has no caller. The web's kept share reaches households through poor-roads-to-prices on business prices (finance-state.ts), so the repair cost is charged once.
replacement: A roads engine (or a budget line that calls setRoadCondition) that owns the poor share and multiplies it by webFactorFor.

whatItFakes: Shifting highway money to transit moves transit service (vehicle revenue miles per resident); the service is kept only in the web.
why: No transit agency or service record exists; the service change reaches riders through transit-service-to-ridership into the trips each household takes (place-prices.ts).
replacement: A transit agency record of service miles that the service link's factor multiplies.

whatItFakes: A federal rail expansion raises intercity rail riders per 1,000 residents.
why: The core has no intercity rail service, station or fare, so there is nothing to carry the rider count.
replacement: An intercity rail engine whose boardings per place multiply by webFactorFor(rail.intercity-ridership).

whatItFakes: Student-debt relief and an abortion denial each move households' past-due debt.
why: The abortion link's cause is a person event the game does not record; the student-debt link has no size or unit until a bill sets the terms. Credit keeps past-due loans but no household record these causes write to.
replacement: A recorded denial event and a student-loan balance on the household that credit.ts past-due loans can read.

whatItFakes: A severe disaster raises a place's non-disaster public transfers.
why: Disasters are recorded (disasters.ts) but transfers are not kept by kind, so no engine reads or pays a non-disaster transfer series to scale.
replacement: Budget transfers split by disaster and non-disaster that the disaster link's factor multiplies.
